Subject: SIG: request for subprocessor list and telemetry flows

Hi Markus,

Acme Health is beginning our SIG intake for Redwood in advance of contracting. To complete the standard questionnaire we need a current list of subprocessors and a short description of what telemetry (logs, metrics, error traces) is sent to each third party. In particular please confirm vendor-level details for: AWS (regions used), Datadog, Sentry, Zendesk (support), and any CDNs or analytics vendors.

What we need from you:
- A CSV with columns: vendor, product, purpose, data_types, envs (hosted/dedicated/private), retention, contractual basis (SLA/BAA), and a contact.
- Links to any SOC2/SIG evidence or subprocessors addenda (or a note if they are included in customer-facing contracts).
- Requested delivery: preliminary CSV by Oct 22, final evidence bundle by Oct 29.

If you have a helpful template we can use to speed review, that would be appreciated.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Julia Smith
Head of Security, Acme Health

Julia — thanks, attaching the inventory per your CSV spec. This is the preliminary export; we'll follow with evidence links. Highlights below and notes inline in the CSV.

Attachment: redwood_subprocessors_oct19.csv (CSV)
CSV columns: vendor, product, purpose, data_types, envs, retention_default, contractual_basis, contact, evidence_link

Quick summary:
- Cloud: AWS (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 failover) — EC2/EBS, S3 for model artifacts and customer logs (where customers enable upload). Retention: depends on customer config, default 30 days for request logs, 90 days for metrics aggregates. Contractual basis: standard customer TOS + optional Data Processing Addendum (DPA) / subprocessor clause.
- Telemetry: Datadog (metrics), Sentry (error/traces). Datadog receives aggregated metrics and environment tags; Sentry receives error traces and stack context. Both have retention controls — we use 90 days default for Sentry error data; Datadog metrics retention varies by metric resolution (see CSV).
- Support: Zendesk (ticket data). PII in support tickets depends on what users submit; customers may redact. Retention: Zendesk default retention; we surface ticket exports when requested.
- Analytics/CDN: Fastly for model artifacts CDN (configurable by region), Mixpanel for non-sensitive product analytics (opt-in).

Evidence and links included in the CSV evidence_link column point to a read-only Drive folder with our SOC2 report, subprocessors addendum template, and vendor contracts where permitted. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-redwood/abcd1234

If you want, we can (a) produce a short attestation letter on Redwood letterhead confirming the list and retention defaults, and (b) provide a redacted vendor contract excerpt showing subprocessor obligations. Which would be most helpful?

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Security & Compliance Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom — I downloaded the CSV and it looks good for a first pass. A couple of quick clarifications we need before moving the SIG questionnaire forward:

- Sentry: can you confirm that error traces are retained for 90 days by default and whether sampling filters are applied to reduce PII in traces?
- Contractual proof: would a signed subprocessors addendum or an attestation letter meet your DPA requirements, or do you require redacted contract excerpts showing flow-down language?

If you can reply to those two points and include the attestation letter you mentioned, we should be able to close the SIG vendor matrix portion. If needed I can loop in our contracting counsel — we are aiming to close this by Oct 29.

Appreciate the fast response.

—Julia
